title: Developing Learning Outcomes
text:
Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development
Developing Learning Outcomes
 Integrating Core Competencies and Values
 Why Education?
 Education is a major tool of addressing and meeting societal needs.
 National Goals of Education are a reflection of the needs of the Kenya
 society.
 National goals of Education are statements that describe the aspirations of
 a country and the needs of the society that are to be met through education.
 Kenya has 8 National Goals of Education. (which are they?)
 Attainment of the National Goals of Education contributes to the overall
 development of the country.
 CBC IN ACHIEVEMENT OF NATIONAL GOALS OF
 EDUCATION
 Kenya embraced the Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) which
 focuses on acquisition of the desired knowledge, skills, values and
 attitudes to enable the learner to cope with life challenges.
 CBC focuses on the achievement of learning outcomes in terms of
 the desired behavioral change. Learning outcomes are derived from
 the National goals of education.
 LEARNING OUTCOMES
 Learning outcomes are the end result or what the learner is able to
 demonstrate upon completion of a lesson, sub-strand, strand or level.
 Express what a learner is expected to do after going through a learning
 experience.
 Focus on what the learner has achieved rather than the intentions of the
 teacher.
 Indicate the expected observable behavioral changes in the learner after
 a learning experience.
 Expressed through the application of knowledge, skills and attitudes.
 Designing learning outcomes
 The CBC is founded on learners showing or demonstrating that they
 have learnt.
 There should be evidence that learning has taken place.
 Learning outcomes are the evidence that learning experiences have
 made a change that learners manifest.
 The change or transformation in learners is manifested through new
 knowledge, skills and attitudes.
 Designing learning outcomes
 Learning outcomes are written with a focus on all the levels of
 thinking. If written without considering the suitable order of thinking for
 the level, this could limit learning and result in a lack of intellectual
 challenge for the learner. taxonomy
 Writing of specific learning outcomes is guided by Taxonomies in
 Education such as the Bloom’s Taxonomy which classifies
 educational learning objectives into three domains, that is, cognitive,
 affective and psychomotor.
Competencies and values are key elements of a learning outcome.
A learning outcome must develop the following:
• Knowledge: acquisition of facts, ideas, concepts; their application,
 synthesis to get new ideas and evaluation of the information.
• Skills: using the knowledge acquired, a learner is able to apply it to
 perform certain tasks against a given standard. The standard to which a
 learner should perform the task is referred to as a competence.
• Values: desirable beliefs and personal attributes that a learner acquires
 through knowledge and skill that influence performance.
 Writing a learning outcome
Statement of a learning outcome should have:
  The action verb
  The object
  The context
 Begin each learning outcome with an ACTION VERB, that will clearly
 illustrate what action learners need to engage in to demonstrate their
 competencies.
 The action could demonstrate a change at the level of knowledge, a skill or
 an attitude.
 The verb in a learning outcome
Verbs such as; identify, name and list.. illustrate knowledge. Example;
By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to :
a) a) identify commonly used punctuation marks in written texts for effective
 communication
b) b) use commas and question marks correctly in written texts for clarity of
 writing
c) c) appreciate the role of punctuation marks for clarity in writing.
The verbs represent the three domains of learning i.e. knowledge, skills
and attitudes.
 The object in learning outcome
The learning outcome also has an OBJECT, which answers the
question “what”
By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify commonly used punctuation marks in written texts for
 effective communication
b) use commas and question marks correctly in written texts for clarity
 of writing
c) appreciate the role of punctuation marks for clarity in writing.
 The context in a learning outcome
The outcome also has a CONTEXT, which answers the question “why”,
“where”, ‘’how” and “when”
By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify commonly used punctuation marks in written texts for effective
 communication
b) use commas and question marks correctly in written texts for clarity of
 writing.
c) appreciate the role of punctuation marks for clarity in writing.
 What characterizes a good learning outcome?
 A good learning outcome begins with an action verb, followed by the
 object of the verb and a phrase that gives the context.
 Preferably only one verb is used in a learning outcome.
 The learning outcomes should be observable.
 Capable of being assessed.
 Does NOT use vague terms such as; know, understand, learn, be
 familiar with, be exposed to, be acquainted with, and be aware of.
 Categories of learning outcomes
 Basic Education is organized into 3 levels. Can you remember them?
 Each level has its own learning outcomes referred to as Level
 learning outcomes derived from the National Goals of Education.
 They are stated in general and broad terms. The essence is to ensure
 that at the end of a given level, the learner has acquired a specific set
 of knowledge, skills and values.
 By the end of the Middle School Education, the learner should be able
 to communicate appropriately using verbal and/or non-verbal modes.
 General learning outcomes
 General learning outcomes, stated in general terms, are derived from
 level learning outcomes.
 Indicate what the learner is expected to achieve in a given learning
 area by the end of a level.
 Which are the learning areas in Middle school?
 Refer to the Curriculum designs for General learning outcomes of
 different learning areas in Middle school).
 Specific learning outcomes
 Specific learning outcomes are geared towards achieving the general
 learning outcomes. Curriculum design is organised in strands and sub
 strands with specific learning outcomes.
 Specify what the learner should know (cognitive), be able to do
 (psychomotor) and demonstrate values (affective) after completing a given
 strand/sub strand or lesson.
 Written from the learners' perspective, can be observed and assessed.
(Refer to the middle school curriculum and identify a specific learning outcome
in a learning area of choice).
Relationship of Learning outcomes
 Activity 1
In groups, analyse the following learning outcomes and comment on
how they have been formulated.
By the end of the sub strand, the learner should be able to:
a) identify four primary colours
b) understand painting materials
c) mix two primary colours to get a secondary colour
d) enjoy mixing different colours.
 Activity 2
Refer to the Middle school level curriculum design, and develop
lesson specific learning outcomes for a sub strand of your
choice.
Share with colleagues and critique each others’ specific learning
outcome.
 Summary
 Level, general and specific learning outcomes, work progressively towards attainment of the National
 Goals of Education.
 Learning outcomes focus on results of the learning experiences and a projection of what we expect,
 reflect the desired end of the learning experience, not the means or the process;
 Linked to assessment as they define what learners are expected to demonstrate.
 Begin each learning outcome with an ACTION VERB, followed by the OBJECT OF THE VERB
 followed by a PHRASE THAT GIVES THE CONTEXT.
 Preferably use only one verb per learning outcome.
 Avoid vague terms like know, understand, learn, be familiar with, be exposed to, be acquainted
 with, and be aware of.
 The learning outcomes must be observable.
 Ensure that the learning outcomes are capable of being assessed.
